newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq workers clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq workers clash with police.

text.p: Ten people were injured, one of them seriously, on Friday when nearly 1,000 workers from bankrupt Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq clashed with police during an impromptu protest action.
Five police trucks were also damaged as workers driving bulldozers and brandishing iron bars tried to block the E19 motorway to Paris south of Brussels.
Reuters photographer Olivier Hoslet saw police turn water cannon on the workers, fire teargas and baton-charge them.
The demonstration broke up after the clashes which lasted about 15 minutes, and workers returned to the Clabecq plant some seven km (four miles) away.
Clabecq workers have staged sporadic protests since the company was declared bankrupt in January.
On Friday their numbers were swelled by colleagues from French carmaker Renault's plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels.
Renault said last month it would close the profitable Vilvoorde plant in July, with the loss of 3,100 jobs, and transfer the work to plants in France and Spain.
Renault workers from all three countries have also staged protests in Belgium and France.
